# My Journey With Neurodiversity

> **Unmasking, reframing thirty years of lived experience, and discovering AuDHD as an adult.**

Receiving a late-in-life diagnosis of ADHD at 31 and Autism at 32 completely reframed how I view my childhood, career, hobbies, and social interactions.

## The Reality of High-Functioning Masking

For decades, intelligence and heavy adaptation allowed me to mask neurodivergent traits. In school and workplace environments, I could analyze expectation patterns and mimic social norms, but the hidden cost was chronic nervous system exhaustion.

## Key Milestones & Insights

- **The April 2025 Turning Point**: Experiencing severe autistic burnout led to formal ADHD evaluation and treatment.
- **When ADHD Medication Cleared the Noise**: As stimulant medication quieted ADHD restlessness, core autistic sensory and routine needs became far more distinct.
- **Autigender & Identity**: Understanding how neurodivergence influences identity and a sense of belonging in modern social discussions.
- **Designing Supportive Systems**: Transforming home lab routines, maker projects, and digital gardens into supportive environments built around natural focus patterns.

Billy Talent has been my favourite band for most of my life.

I started listening to them in 2005 when I was 12 years old. Their music quickly became the soundtrack to many of my teenage years, and over time they became much more than just another band I enjoyed listening to.

One year in music class, I chose Billy Talent as the subject of a presentation. Researching the band taught me about each member, their history, and the stories behind many of their songs and lyrics. It was one of the first times I remember diving deeply into the people behind the music I loved.

My aunt took me to see Billy Talent in St. John's while she was pregnant with her first child. illScarlett opened for them, making it one of my earliest live concert experiences.

Since then, I've seen Billy Talent perform multiple times at the Iceberg Alley Performance Tent. Each time I watched from the JAG Sky Bar VIP section.

The first two concerts featured Aaron Solowoniuk performing alongside the band for a few songs. By the third concert he was no longer performing live, making each show feel like a different chapter in the band's history.

One memory from that final concert has stayed with me.

I was dancing, jumping, singing, and simply enjoying being at a rock concert. Nearby was a group of people who appeared to be more interested in having conversations than watching the show. Later, one of my friends mentioned that they seemed irritated by how much fun I was having and kept giving me strange looks.

At the time I didn't think much of it.

Looking back, especially after learning more about myself as an adult, that moment feels different. It reminds me how differently people experience the same event. For me, concerts are meant to be immersive, energetic experiences. For others, they can simply be another social gathering.

It's a small memory, but one that now connects music, identity, and the way people experience the world differently.

I discovered Bo Burnham at a very young age

I was using YouTube on a regular basis since 2006

I always admired and looked up to Bo as a kid

I specifically watched YouTube live in 2007 because I wanted to see Bo's performance

I followed him his whole career

His content really resonates with me

I tried submitting "High School Party" as my yearbook "song" submission. Unfortunatly the teachers looked up the lyrics beforehand...

I watched his special, Words Words Words, before I knew where the reference came from. I would figure out that year though because Hamlet was our grade 12 Shakespeare study

Still on board. Then, "what." came out. This is when Bo starts being more creative with his artwork and gives us a glimpse at how he is as a person. Before then, "art is dead" was probably the only thing that had anything "meaningful" behind it. 

I can't remember if this is the time he was posting on Vine, but they were also things I looked up to and tried to imitate to some degree.

Make Happy is a hard one for me, because it came out the same year I started getting treated for depression. There is also a pretty triggering song that used to get stuck in my head (ear worms) that I had to avoid watching or listening to it too much. He expands on what he did with "what." in a sense that he gives us even more of his honest work rather than his performative work.

I'll admit, I skupped Eighth Grade. I think at the time, and maybe still now, it would hit too close to home. 

The last special he has put out, Inside, again forthers the theme of Bo's content getting more and more personal as time goes on.

And that brings us to present day. I use Bo as a stim tool now, because listening to his music makes me happy. It's a familiar voice who has unknowingly to him, or myself, that led me through adolesense, followed me into my early adult life, and now is still lingering as I go into my 30s. Canada Fluorspar has played a major role in my professional life.

I first joined the mine in 2017 after leaving my job at Dairy Queen to pursue an opportunity in industry.

Before I could even begin, I failed my pre-employment drug test. I waited a month, tried again, and passed.

My first contract eventually ended, and I found myself effectively blacklisted from returning to site.

For the next two years I continued trying to get back.

Eventually one of the project managers hired me almost on the spot. Human Resources wasn't convinced and required another interview before approving my return. I had to overcome the reputation that had followed me from my first employment.

Once back on site, my career evolved quickly.

I returned in the same position I had previously held before moving into a Junior Project Engineer role.

Later I became a Junior Mine Engineer.

After that I transitioned into Mobile Maintenance Planner.

When the company entered receivership, I lost my job only five days before my son was born.

In 2024 I returned once again under the new ownership, this time as an IT Technician.

Within roughly six months I was promoted to IT Coordinator, a role that finally allowed me to combine my engineering background with my passion for technology, systems, and problem solving.

My story with Canada Fluorspar is still being written.

# My Story With Healthcare: Advocacy, Trauma, & Systemic Failures

> **Healthcare is a double-edged sword—capable of delivering life-changing breakthroughs, yet capable of profound systemic coldness when empathy is needed most.**

My experiences with the healthcare system have included both the best and most difficult moments of my life. From dealing with physical health issues as a child to discovering late-in-life neurodiversity, surviving a horrific NICU experience, and managing severe sleep apnea, navigating medical systems has required constant self-advocacy.

---

## 1. Childhood Stigma & Early Health Challenges

Growing up, my physical health journey started with weight issues following a toddler illness. Stigma followed me early on. Moving to Carbonear in 1999 at six years old, I distinctly remember playing outside with neighborhood kids when a peer openly laughed and made derogatory comments about my body. Putting on a brave face to keep my cool became a habit early in life.

Beyond weight, physical health issues mounted:
- **Vision Misdiagnosis**: My parents were initially told my eyesight was fine. A second opinion in Carbonear revealed my eyes were only as developed as a two-year-old's, requiring immediate corrective lenses.
- **Macular Edema**: In the summer of 2010, after a routine contact lens follow-up, my left eye suddenly went completely blurry. As the youngest person in the waiting room by four decades, I was rushed to the Janeway Children’s Hospital emergency room. By 2016, vision distortions began affecting my right eye as well.
- **Physical Complications**: Chronic ear infections required repeated antibiotic courses, alongside painful hereditary ingrown toenail procedures.

---

## 2. Mental Health, Panic Attacks, & The 7-Year Waitlist

Mental health care in Newfoundland has been a complex journey. 

In the fall of 2015, I sought help for severe depression at a walk-in clinic, receiving a temporary prescription while waiting for a family doctor. By 2017, while working at Dairy Queen, a verbal confrontation with an aggressive customer triggered my first major panic attack. Visiting the psychiatric emergency department led to a medication change that finally brought mental clarity.

```text
2015: Initial Depression Treatment (Walk-in Clinic)
  └──> 2017: Dairy Queen Panic Attack & Psychiatric Care
        └──> April 2025: Autistic Burnout & ADHD Evaluation
              └──> Present: Identifying as AuDHD (7+ Year Public Waitlist)
```

The real turning point came in **April 2025**. Following a mental health breakdown and years of burnout, I received an ADHD evaluation. Starting ADHD medication helped manage executive dysfunction, but as the mental noise quieted, my Autistic traits became significantly more prominent.

Today, I live and identify as **AuDHD (Autistic + ADHD)**. In Newfoundland and Labrador, the public health waitlist for an official adult autism diagnosis is currently **7+ years**.

> **Systemic Advocacy Note**: If you suspect your child is Autistic, seek early intervention immediately. Early intervention must extend beyond obvious presentations to include **twice-exceptional (2e)** individuals who mask well. Adult diagnostic access in Canada requires urgent reform.

---

## 3. The CPAP Breakthrough & Vision Recovery

For years, I suffered from severe, undiagnosed sleep apnea—a condition running on my father's side of the family. When I finally completed a sleep study, the results were alarming:

* **Apnea Index**: Over **60 apnea events per hour** (severe sleep apnea).
* **Oxygen Desaturation**: Blood oxygen levels plummeting into the **60s** during sleep.
* **Licensure Risk**: Motor Vehicle Division warned my driver's license would be revoked without immediate treatment.

Starting **CPAP (Continuous Positive Airway Pressure) therapy** transformed my life overnight. The extreme daytime drowsiness while driving vanished, and I stopped waking up constantly in the middle of the night wide awake.

Remarkably, starting CPAP therapy directly coincided with my long-standing **macular edema going away**. After fifteen years of specialist follow-ups, my ophthalmologist confirmed the edema had fully subsided. Restoring proper nighttime oxygen saturation allowed my eyes to heal.

---

## 4. Trauma in the NICU & A Broken Support System

The most painful experience with healthcare occurred during the birth of my son.

During delivery, my son suffered **shoulder dystocia**, resulting in a collapsed lung. When he was born, he came out completely blue and did not change color. He was immediately wheeled out of the delivery room without explanation.

```text
Delivery Room: Shoulder Dystocia & Collapsed Lung
  └──> 2 Hours of Agonizing Silence (No Updates)
        └──> Medical Intervention: 10 mL Air Syringed from Chest
              └──> Transfer to NICU in St. John's
```

My partner and I were left waiting in agonizing silence for **nearly two hours** before a doctor finally returned to inform us what was happening. The physician had to manually syringe 10 mL of trapped air from his chest before transferring him to the Neonatal Intensive Care Unit (NICU) in St. John's.

As scared, exhausted first-time parents, our experience with NICU nursing staff was deeply distressing:
- **Disrespect & Scolding**: After being instructed by doctors to wait until morning rounds before entering, nurses scolded us upon arrival, snapping *"Baby needs to eat, you know."*
- **Lack of Feeding Empathy**: When our son developed jaundice, nursing staff pressured us to switch from breastfeeding to formula, but refused to state it directly, showing zero empathy for my partner's struggles with nursing.
- **Emotional Exhaustion**: We ultimately switched to formula, navigating post-traumatic stress without support.

---

## 5. Corporate Coldness in the Hospital Room

Compounding the NICU trauma, **five days prior to my son's birth**, Canada Fluorspar Inc. (CFI)—the mining company where I worked as IT Coordinator—suddenly entered receivership.

I lost my job overnight with zero notice, zero severance, and no closure.

While sitting in the hospital room holding my newborn son in the NICU, I received an email from CFI Human Resources claiming they had tried to contact me (despite zero missed calls) and informing me that I needed to come to the mine site to collect my personal belongings.

The complete absence of empathy from corporate management during a family medical emergency was appalling.

---

## 6. Reflections & Moving Forward

Navigating physical illness, adult AuDHD, sleep apnea recovery, and parental trauma has taught me that healthcare cannot function on clinical algorithms alone—it requires human empathy.

By sharing this story behind subscriber tiers, I hope to advocate for:
1. **Twice-Exceptional Awareness**: Recognizing neurodivergence early before burnout occurs.
2. **Adult Diagnostic Reform**: Shortening multi-year waitlists for adult Autism and ADHD assessments.
3. **Compassionate Patient Care**: Reminding healthcare providers that first-time parents in crisis deserve dignity, respect, and clear communication.

# My Story With IT Coordination & Industrial Mining Infrastructure

> **Managing IT for a remote industrial mining operation means wrestling with legacy hardware, unravelling MSP incompetence, surviving ransomware attacks, and keeping critical infrastructure online when everything is stacked against you.**

When I stepped into the role of IT Coordinator at **Canada Fluorspar Inc. (CFI)** in St. Lawrence, Newfoundland, I knew industrial technology presented unique challenges. What I didn't expect was inheriting a network infrastructure held together by legacy compromises, zero documentation, and third-party vendors treating the company as an open checkbook.

---

## 1. Inheriting the Chaos: Cable Spanning & Missing Keys

My first weeks as IT Coordinator were spent uncovering the reality of the site's physical infrastructure. 

Instead of an organized, documented enterprise network, I walked into complete chaos:
- **Zero Documentation**: No network topology diagrams, no IP allocation tables, and no historical records of configuration changes.
- **Switches on Locked Boxes**: Network switches were literally sitting on top of their dedicated wall-mounted lockboxes because previous personnel had lost the keys.
- **The Backwards Rack**: The main distribution switch rack supplying network connectivity across the entire industrial facility had been installed **backwards and too close to the wall**, forcing network cables into an unmanageable, tangled bird's nest.
- **Analog Radio Limitations**: Mine operations relied on aging analog/digital radio repeaters. Despite my constant pitches to executive management advocating for a modern digital radio migration for safety and clarity, cost-cutting priorities repeatedly shelved the project.

```text
CFI Site Network Distribution:
  ├── Mill & Crusher Operations (High Dust / Vibration)
  ├── Geology & Mine Extraction (Field Laptops & Radio Mesh)
  ├── Environment & Safety Monitoring (Real-Time Sensor Feeds)
  └── Admin, HR, & Site Services (Core ERP & Corporate Traffic)
```

---

## 2. Managing IT Across Eight Industrial Departments

Unlike corporate offices where IT supports standardized desktop workstations, an industrial mine site operates as a collection of mini-enterprises. 

As IT Coordinator, I was single-handedly responsible for the IT budget, roadmap, hardware procurement, and daily support for eight distinct departments:
1. **Mining Operations**: Heavy machinery telemetry and ruggedized field units.
2. **Mill Operations**: High-vibration processing plant networking.
3. **Crusher Operations**: Dust-heavy industrial control environments.
4. **Geology**: High-bandwidth spatial mapping and core sample data.
5. **Safety**: Emergency radio systems and incident reporting.
6. **Environment**: Environmental compliance sensor arrays.
7. **Site Services**: Camp facility logistics and connectivity.
8. **HR & Administration**: Payroll, corporate ERP, and personnel records.

On top of long-term budget planning, I faced constant **interruption fatigue**—expected to drop high-priority infrastructure work instantly to resolve ad-hoc daily user issues across the entire property.

---

## 3. Exposing MSP Incompetence: The 3-Month Internet Throttling Nightmare

Prior to taking full internal control of IT coordination, CFI relied heavily on a Managed Service Provider (MSP). 

Between mine operations starting in 2024 and my transition into IT in 2025, the original MSP (**Atlantic Data**) was acquired by a larger corporation (**Vision 33**). The primary engineers we relied on left during the merger, and Vision 33 began treating CFI as an open checkbook—billing substantial monthly retainers while delivering sub-par technical oversight.

```text
The 3-Month Firewall Mystery:
  Vision 33 Incompetence ──> Misconfigured Firewall Rule
                             └──> Blocked Microsoft Windows Update Traffic
                                   └──> Hundreds of Endpoint Retries
                                         └──> Site-Wide Internet Throttled for 90 Days!
```

The depth of this incompetence became undeniable during a **three-month site-wide network slowdown**. Operations across the entire mine were choked as internet speeds crawled to a near standstill. Vision 33 blamed local ISPs, bandwidth caps, and infrastructure limitations. 

After ninety days of frustration, Vision 33 was forced to hire an external independent consultant to investigate. The consultant discovered the root cause within hours: **a misconfigured firewall rule created by Vision 33 itself that blocked Microsoft Windows Update downloads**. 

Because endpoints were blocked from completing updates, hundreds of site devices were endlessly retrying in the background, saturating the entire mine site's internet connection.

---

## 4. April 2025: Surviving the Akira Ransomware Attack

In **April 2025**, CFI faced its most dangerous technical crisis: a targeted cyberattack by the notorious **Akira Ransomware** group.

```text
Akira Cyberattack Vector:
  [Akira Threat Actors] ──> Infiltrated Enterprise Network
                             ├── Encrypted Domain Controllers
                             ├── Encrypted File Servers & Shares
                             └── FAILED to Encrypt Datto Backup Appliance!
                                   └── [FAST RECOVERY & ZERO RANSOM PAID]
```

Akira threat actors breached the network perimeter, elevating privileges and executing encryption scripts across domain controllers, administrative shares, and core infrastructure. 

The ONLY reason Canada Fluorspar Inc. survived without paying a ransom or suffering catastrophic permanent data loss was our **Datto backup appliance**. Akira's automated scripts failed to compromise or encrypt the hardened Datto appliance. 

Working relentlessly under immense pressure, we isolated the infected segments, wiped the compromised servers, and executed bare-metal restores directly from our Datto image backups.

---

## 5. Server Battles & Infrastructure Realities

Throughout my tenure, maintaining server stability required constant battles with executive management. 

Our physical server fleet was aging rapidly, suffering hardware degradation. When proposing essential server hardware refreshes or hybrid cloud migrations, management routinely pushed back, arguing that *"a single virtual server would be good enough"* to run the entire mine's workload.

Explaining the realities of hypervisor resource allocation, IOPS bottlenecks, and redundancy to non-technical executives who viewed IT purely as a cost center was an ongoing hurdle.

---

## 6. Takeaways & The Vision for Keel Systems

Wrestling with un-documented networks, surviving Akira ransomware, exposing predatory MSP retainer billing, and managing industrial IT across eight mine site departments reinforced key engineering principles:

1. **Infrastructure Independence**: Never outsource core network architecture without internal oversight.
2. **Immutable Offsite Backups**: Hardened, air-gapped backup appliances (like Datto) are the difference between corporate survival and total collapse.
3. **Pragmatic Systems Design**: Documentation, proper rack orientation, and clean cable management are operational safety requirements—not cosmetic luxuries.

This intense industrial experience laid the groundwork for my future consulting firm, **Keel Systems**—building resilient, documented, and honest technology solutions for organizations that cannot afford downtime.

# My Story With Neurodiversity, Adult Diagnosis, & Autigender

> **High-functioning masking is an intellectual marathon. Brute-forcing a Mechanical Engineering degree without knowing you're neurodivergent works until the internal engine collapses into Autistic Burnout.**

Receiving an ADHD diagnosis at age 31 and an Autism diagnosis at age 32 brought thirty years of unexplained struggles into sharp focus. For three decades, I navigated education, social dynamics, and careers with an undiagnosed neurodivergent brain—relying on high intelligence to compensate for hidden neurological strain.

---

## 1. High IQ & Social Brute-Forcing

Growing up twice-exceptional (2e), masking was not an intuitive social skill; it was a conscious, analytical algorithm:
- **Social Mistake Cataloging**: Whenever I made a social blunder or experienced an awkward interaction, I mentally cataloged the mistake, analyzing the variables so I could explicitly avoid repeating it in future interactions.
- **Academic Brute-Forcing**: Having a high IQ allowed me to "brute-force" my way through primary school, post-secondary education, and earn a rigorous **Mechanical Engineering degree** without formal study systems or early neurodivergent accommodations.

```text
High-IQ Masking Algorithm:
  Social Interaction ──> Awkwardness / Mistake ──> Mental Error Analysis
                                                          │
  Academic Success <── Brute-Force Intellect <── Cataloged Behavioral Rule
```

While brute-forcing got me through engineering school and into technical careers, the cognitive overhead of constant real-time social computation was accumulating interest behind the scenes.

---

## 2. When ADHD Calmed Down, Autistic Traits Grew Louder

In **April 2025**, the dam broke. Years of unrelenting compensation culminated in severe **Autistic Burnout**. 

Working with mental health professionals led to initiating ADHD medication. But as stimulant therapy successfully quieted the restless ADHD "noise," my underlying Autistic traits became significantly more prominent:

```text
Pre-Treatment (ADHD Restlessness Masks Autism)
  ├── Constant Mental Noise & Impulse
  └── High Sensory Threshold (Chaos Distracts Chaos)

Post-Treatment (ADHD Quieted by Medication)
  ├── 🔊 Sensory Sensitivities Heightened (Bright Lights, Loud Audio)
  ├── 🔒 Rigid Routine Preferences Required
  ├── 🎯 Intense Hyperfocus Tracks
  └── 🔋 Hard Social Energy Caps (Rapid Battery Depletion)
```

Therapy confirmed that I was experiencing classic Autistic Burnout. Today, I am actively working through recovery using resources like *Unmasking Autism* by Dr. Devon Price and *The Autism Burnout Recovery Workbook*, unlearning decades of unhealthy suppression.

---

## 3. Childhood Intuition & Non-Conforming Curiosity

Reading *Unmasking Autism* introduced me to the concept of **Autigender**—how Autistic cognitive processing alters a person's relationship to societal gender expectations and rigid social constructs.

Looking back at childhood, my interests frequently crossed traditional 1990s gender boundaries:
- **The Easy-Bake Oven**: As a child, I desperately wanted an Easy-Bake Oven. It wasn't because I identified as a girl; I simply loved the idea of baking and eating fresh cookies and cakes. My dad refused to get me one, fearing it would make me "gay"—a reflection of rigid 90s gender tropes.
- **Kindergarten Nurturing**: In kindergarten, my favourite activity was taking home the class teddy bear and caring for it—a tender, nurturing trait that defied masculine stereotypes of the era.
- **Anatomical Confusion**: Prior to puberty, pubic fat stores made my anatomy appear smaller, and I noticed the scrotal raphe line. Intuiting as a young child, I thought: *"This line looks like it was sewn together... was I supposed to be a girl?"* At one point I taped my anatomy down, but after using the bathroom realized how silly it was and snapped out of it. 

I didn't think much about that childhood event again for over two decades—until discovering how Autistic children interpret physical bodies and social roles through literal, curious logic.

---

## 4. Autigender, Belonging, & The Risk of Misdiagnosis

Understanding **Autigender** offers vital perspective on modern discussions surrounding identity, youth, and belonging.

```text
Isolated / Undiagnosed Autistic Youth (Searching for Belonging)
  ├── Non-Conforming Interests + Literal Body Intuition
  ├── Social Alienation / Lack of Peer Connections
  └── Risk of Medical Misdiagnosis vs. True Neurodivergent Unmasking (AuDHD)
```

As a 32-year-old adult, I reflect on what might have happened had I been born twenty years later in 2013. If an isolated, undiagnosed Autistic kid searching for peer belonging were exposed to online spaces where medical transition is presented as the primary answer to social alienation, I might have been convinced to pursue permanent medical transition.

Looking back now, I recognize that would have been a catastrophic misdiagnosis for what was fundamentally **undiagnosed AuDHD, high-IQ masking, and Autigender non-conformity**.

---

## 5. Unmasking & Moving Forward

True self-acceptance at 32 means embracing neurodivergence without needing to force myself into rigid boxes:
1. **Honoring Social Energy Caps**: Respecting my social battery without feeling guilty for needing solitary recovery time.
2. **Sensory Accommodation**: Designing home lab, studio, and maker environments that accommodate sensory sensitivities.
3. **Open, Nuanced Dialogue**: Advocating for twice-exceptional awareness, early childhood screening, and nuanced conversations about identity that protect vulnerable neurodivergent youth.

# Battery Dispenser & Workshop Storage

> **Gravity-fed, modular battery organization for home workshops.**

## Overview

Over the years, managing rechargeable AA, AAA, and 9V batteries across home lab devices, VR controllers, and workshop tools led to clutter. Instead of buying generic plastic bins, I designed a modular dispenser system manufactured using my **xTool S1 40W Diode Laser** and 3D printers.

## Design Goals & Mechanics

- **Gravity Loading & Dispensing**: Load fresh batteries from the top, draw oldest cells from the bottom tray.
- **Capacity**: Holds 50+ AA/AAA batteries in a compact footprint.
- **No Complex Hardware**: Snap-fit and interlocking finger-joint wood assembly requiring minimal glue.
- **Visual Appeal**: Laser-etched battery indicators and slate-accented base.

## Modular Variants

1. **Variant A (AAA Cells)**: Compact vertical gravity chute for AAA batteries.
2. **Variant B (AA Cells)**: Wide-channel chute designed for high-capacity AA packs.
3. **Variant C (Combo Modular)**: Dual-chamber dispenser with removable 3D-printed battery dividers.

## Commercial Plans

Once final tolerances are verified, vector SVG cutting templates and 3D STL files will be packaged for digital download on Etsy and maker platforms.

Reflecting on taking Gender Studies in university, the course curriculum primarily focused on Women's Studies rather than a broad, multi-dimensional analysis of gender constructs across society.

## University Classroom Observations

One of the early class discussions centered on analyzing an engineering student event slogan (*"D-Day"*—an engineering tradition held on the first Friday of each semester). While most students understood the wordplay context, the lecture framework pushed a single rigid interpretation, demonstrating how academic discourse often enforces ideological consensus over open discussion.

## Modern Rhetoric & The Nuance of Pay Gaps

In modern political discourse, topics like the gender pay gap are often presented without essential statistical variables. When comparing raw averages without accounting for occupational risk, dangerous working conditions, overtime hours, and parental leave choices, complex economic discussions get reduced to simplistic slogans. 

As a neurodivergent and disabled individual who has navigated systemic hurdles firsthand, I value nuanced, data-driven dialogue over partisan rhetoric.

# Video Editing & Content Creation

> **Crafting narrative and rhythm through visual cuts.**

Video editing combines storytelling, audio sync, color grading, and motion graphics to create compelling visual media. From editing early gameplay clips to producing polished video walkthroughs, video creation relies on pacing and flow.

## Key Techniques & Focus Areas

- **Nonlinear Editing Tools**: DaVinci Resolve and Adobe Premiere Pro for multi-track editing.
- **Audio Sync & Sound Design**: Matching vocal tracks with background ambiance and kinetic cuts.
- **Visual Storytelling**: Pacing edits to keep viewers engaged while conveying complex technical concepts cleanly.
